To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
toxicity of nickel on selected marine diatoms and marine copepods was determined and species mean chronic values were derived using SSD method.
nickel is toxic to diatoms and copepod and the species mean chronic values for nickel on diatoms are 0.016 and 0.17 mg/L and for copepods are 0.57–0.42 µg/L. The
toxicity values were derived for nickel based on bioassays with marine diatoms and marine copepods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of toxicity values for the selected species of diatoms and copepod for the protection of plankton community in the coastal and marine ecosystems of India.
the toxicity assessment of nickel to marine diatoms and zooplankton species.
the assessment of the toxicity of nickel on selected species of diatoms and copepod in marine water.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the toxicity values of nickel on marine diatom and copepod are 13.3 × 10−2 mg/L and 1.33 × 10–2 mg/L, which is almost an order of difference.
nickel is toxic to marine diatoms and planktonic copepods and the toxicity of nickel to copepods is less than diatoms.
nickel is toxic to marine organisms and the toxicity values obtained from the bioassay tests may be utilized for the derivation of water quality criteria.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the toxicity of nickel is species specific, and it is important to use the species specific values for the assessment of the toxicity of nickel in the coastal waters.
the toxicity of nickel to the selected marine species is in the order of copepods > diatoms and the derived toxicity values may be useful for the development of water quality guidelines.

diatoms are more sensitive than copepods to nickel and the species mean toxicity values for nickel are 2–3 times higher for marine plankton species of India compared to the toxicity values reported from other countries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
diatoms are more sensitive than copepods.
the diatom species are more sensitive to the nickel pollution than the copepods.
diatoms are more sensitive than copepods to nickel and the toxicity values derived in this study may be used to calculate ambient water criteria for nickel in coastal and marine waters of India.
